title: HYDRON MARITIME: SATELLITE OPTICAL NETWORK EXTENSION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.239) EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept evolving HydRON services to maritime communications and identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap.Targeted Improvements:To enable maritime communications with satellite HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) systemDescription:Maritime routes are strategic in a connected world, where economies are interdependent. 80% of the global trade depends on shipping. Current strategical routes include South China, South India, Suez Canal, Mediterranean see, trans-Atlantic and Panama Canal. Together with the current routes, the transit along the arctic seais currently becoming more attention for cargo ships but also for defence purposes. Climate change may enable the use of this route,which could mean a drastic reduction in transport costs and service time (reduction of 25-40% in distance). From a logistics perspective, cargo companies aim to monitor their goods and containers, while ports seek to receive advance information about incoming cargo to optimize and plan the unloading process.Additional to the commercial and logistic interests, the defence aspects connected to maritime communications are of special interest, especially in an arctic route, where any developed infrastructure, could enhanceresilience.Currently, maritime communications relay on low-data rate satellite communications, or the use of low-band frequencies, when the ships are located close to shore. HydRON provides space-space and space-ground connectivity, extending terrestrial networksin space and providing global coverage.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements and system concepts for maritimecommunications (space-sea, sea-sea, sea-shore/ports), to extend the use of HydRON in maritime scenarios. Technology gaps and related technology roadmaps shall be developed, considering optical terminals and any critical technologies. The system shall consider themanagement of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a maritime ship-to-ship free-space network or hybrid communications with RF. The space segment shall consider the coverage along the most used routes. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be demonstrated. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

title: S3-CL-03 ERASE PHASE A ACTIVE DEBRIS REMOVAL MISSION FOR LARGE UNPREPARED LEO PLATFORMS - EXPRO+
description: ESA intends to implement a Zero Debris policy by 2030 and has a long-term vision for a sustainable and safe space environment leveraging on the development of a space circular economy.Large Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites in particular present significant risks, both in terms of potential collisions and ground casualty hazards resulting from uncontrolled re-entry.  The ESA's Clean Space Office has been pioneering the study of ADR since 2012, starting with the e.Deorbit study, followed by the ClearSpace-1 and the CAT mission in more recent years, under the ADRIOS initiative part of the ESA Space Safety Program. In the past years there has been growing interest in ADR services targeting large LEO debris objects. This topic has recently been the focus of discussions and studies between ESA and external stakeholders, including EUMETSAT in the frame of a feasibility study (e.g. CDF) and the European Commission(EC) via its ISOS framework. This led to the implementation of industrial activities for a 6 month ERASE phase 0 mission and systemstudy which was kicked-off Q1 of 2026.The activity proposed here is to further mature the concept of the ERASE mission up to the Preliminary Requirement Review (PRR) milestone. The result of the activity and the maturation of the ERASE concept should be in linewith the outcomes of an ESA Preliminary Requirements Review as described by the ECSS. If successful, ESA intends to follow this study by the  Phase B1 and a eventual full mission implementation acceptance after CMin 2028

title: ULTRACOMPACT 778 NM RUBIDIUM SECONDARY OPTICAL FREQUENCY STANDARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop an ultracompact, secondary, optical frequency reference based on a two-photon transition in Rb vapour at 778nm.Description:Ultra-stable miniature atomic clocks are being considered for space applications. The Rubidium two-photon transition secondary frequency standard has demonstrated interesting performance metrics with a further potential for ultra-low size, weight and power (SWaP) integration.Currently, such an approach is hindered by the lack of miniaturized laser sources with suitable power levels and spectral properties as well as a compact physics package design taking advantage of the full capabilities of the integrated photonics and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gas cell technology platforms.This activity aims at exploiting these enabling technologies and developing a further concept of a compact high-performance atomic physics package for an ultra-compact secondary optical frequency standard. The goal of this activity is to provide a fractional frequency stability < 10 - 12 at 1 second integration time implemented using integrated photonic techniques.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Evaluate sources of integrated photonic laser systems delivering the wavelengths and the required spectral properties for the defined system approach. Develop Rb cell techniques and technologies targeting an ultracompact 778 nm rubidium secondary optical frequency standard using chip-scale photonic integration. Demonstrate the fractional stability performance achievable using the chosen chip-scale photonic approach. Evaluate chip-scale optical frequency combs with SiN Kerr comb techniques to provide an initial stabilized direct optical-RF link. Provide a packaging solution to maintain the preliminary performance achieved.NOTE: This activityis currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The finallist of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: EO4SLOVENIA - AN EO BASED SOLUTION FOR NATURAL HAZARDS AND WATER RESOURCES IN SLOVENIA - EXPRO+
description: Water Resources Management (WRM) and Disaster Risk Management (DRM) are two thematic areas that are important in Slovenia. In 2025 a preparatory activity concerning the contribution of satellite data for different thematic areas has highlighted the needs of priorities of a group of nationally mandated stakeholders from both the WRM sector and the DRM sector. While the ESA Digital Twin Earth (ESA DTE) programme is looking at integrating Earth Observation (EO) satellite capabilities in future operational Digital Twins ecosystems, including the potential future evolution of DestinE and other operational DT initiatives in Europe, this activity is a precursor development under the FutureEO programme to prepare the ground for an EO based digital ecosystem and connect EO data, processingchains and modelling. This FutureEO activity aims to implement and demonstrate a preliminary Digital Twin Precursor to prefigure potential EO based Digital Twin developments. This ITT refers to implementing an EO-based Digital Twin precursor for the themes Water Resources Management and Disaster Risk Management for Slovenia identified through community consultation and considered to be mature enough to start a large activity. For both WRM and DRM themes, the project shall deliver end-to-end pre-operational solutions, fullyimplemented, conceptually and technically mature, scientifically validated, and fully tested by a representative set of early adopters.
